notes:
I could only research verses 1–10 properly. My tools hit their usage limit partway through, so for verses 11–27 most notes come from one source, Enduring Word (David Guzik). I couldn't read any Catholic, Orthodox, Lutheran, Pentecostal, Wesleyan or modern-scholarship pages, so section 3 is missing. The NET Bible page loaded the wrong chapter, so there are no NET notes. The tradition labels in brackets (Reformed, Baptist and so on) are my own; the pages don't state them.

---

## John 4:1–27 – Research notes

**v. 1**
- The Pharisees were watching Jesus closely. He left to avoid a fight before His "hour" had come. Blum (Bible Knowledge Commentary) contrasts Nicodemus, a respected and orthodox Jew, with this outcast woman: both still needed new birth. – https://www.preceptaustin.org/john-4-commentary
- Utley (bible.org) sees a deliberate pairing in chapters 3–4: the religious insider and the woman on the margins, official Judaism and Samaritan religion. – https://www.preceptaustin.org/john-4-commentary
- **How did Jesus "know"?** Writers disagree:
  - Jamieson-Fausset-Brown (JFB) and Benson say He knew without being told, as in John 2:25.
  - Meyer says it was ordinary knowledge, since the crowds made the news obvious.
  - Barnes and Poole leave both options open.
  – https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/4-1.htm
- Precept Austin lists three options: Jesus' own divine knowledge, the Father or Spirit told Him, or someone informed Him. – https://www.preceptaustin.org/john-4-commentary
- Ellicott: the second half of the verse gives the report in the words the Pharisees heard it. – https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/4-1.htm

**v. 2**
- **Traditional reading:** this verse corrects the report. Reasons given for why Jesus didn't baptize personally:
  - Preaching mattered more (Matthew Henry, Benson).
  - It avoided people boasting, or splitting into groups, over who baptized them (Barnes, Gill).
  - Christ is the one who baptizes with the Holy Spirit (Ellicott, Bengel, JFB).
  – https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/4-2.htm
- Godet: by leaving water baptism to the apostles, Jesus made it independent of His physical presence, so the church could carry it on after He left. – https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/4-2.htm
- Bible.org (Lesson 21) adds the guess that people might later have boasted "Jesus baptized me." – https://bible.org/seriespage/lesson-21-living-water-thirsty-woman-john-41-14
- **Where traditions differ (what baptism is):**
  - *Calvin [Reformed]:* this baptism counts as Christ's own even though others performed it. Its power depends on its Author, not the minister. – https://www.studylight.org/commentary/john/4-2.html
  - *Precept Austin, citing MacArthur and W. A. Criswell [Baptist/evangelical]:* the verse argues against "baptismal regeneration" (the belief that baptism itself saves). Baptism is an act of obedience and a public witness that cannot save. – https://www.preceptaustin.org/john-4-commentary
  - *Coffman [Churches of Christ]:* anyone baptized by Christ's disciples according to His command "is truly baptized by Jesus." – https://www.studylight.org/commentary/john/4-2.html
- Guzik: the disciples' baptism here was about repentance and pointed ahead to Christian baptism, which began at Pentecost. – https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-4/

**v. 3**
- Benson: Jesus returned to Galilee, where the ruling council had less power, after about eight months in Judea. – https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/4-1.htm
- Precept Austin links the move to John the Baptist's arrest (Matthew 4:12). Harris (bible.org) says the text gives no clear reason. – https://www.preceptaustin.org/john-4-commentary

**v. 4 – "had to"**
- **Geography:** Samaria lay directly between Judea and Galilee (Barnes, Poole, Meyer). Strict Jews took the longer road through Perea (east of the Jordan). – https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/4-4.htm
- **A deeper necessity:** writers frame it differently.
  - Ellicott: going was part of His mission to teach true worship to all nations.
  - Pulpit Commentary: there was no physical need for this road; a "providential monition" (God's prompting) led Him.
  - Gill [Calvinist]: He had to go to call the Samaritans "whom the Father had given to him." Their time for conversion had come.
  - Vincent: there may be a hint of the Father's will, but John doesn't present it as a mission to the Samaritans.
  – https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/4-4.htm
- Guzik: the need was the people there, not the route. – https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-4/
- Spurgeon, Boa and Stedman (quoted by Precept Austin): Jesus felt an inner pull toward the Samaritans and cut through prejudice. – https://www.preceptaustin.org/john_44-15_commentary

**v. 5**
- **Is Sychar the same as Shechem?**
  - Guzik, Poole and JFB say yes. Guzik lists Shechem's Old Testament history (Abram, Jacob, Joseph's bones, Joshua's covenant). He also cites Alford: "Sychar" ("drunken") may have been a Jewish insult. – https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-4/ ; https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/4-5.htm
  - Utley: many assume so, but the New Testament doesn't say it. – https://bible.org/seriespage/john-4
  - Coffman places Sychar *near* Shechem. – https://www.studylight.org/commentary/john/4-5.html
- **The plot of ground:** Genesis 33:19 (land Jacob bought) and 48:22 (land given to Joseph); Joseph's bones were buried there (Joshua 24:32). – https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/4-5.htm ; https://www.gty.org/blogs/B210913/a-strange-encounter-on-sacred-ground

**v. 6**
- **Real tiredness shows Jesus was truly human** (Matthew Henry, Gill, Poole). The word "thus" stresses complete exhaustion: He just sat down wherever He was (Maclaren). – https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/4-6.htm
- Spurgeon: He seems more tired than His disciples, perhaps tired in mind as well as body. Even so, He was waiting to bless her: "a weary Christ" for "a weary sinner." – https://www.spurgeon.org/resource-library/sermons/jesus-sitting-on-the-well/
- **The time:** Barnes, Barclay and Constable say the "sixth hour" was noon. – https://www.studylight.org/commentary/john/4-6.html
  - One quoted sermon on biblehub instead pictures the western sun lengthening the shadows. – https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/4-6.htm

**v. 7**
- **She came alone, at an unusual hour.** Guzik suggests a sudden need or that she was a social outcast. He also cites Bruce: women usually came in groups and at cooler times. – https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-4/
- **Was "Give me a drink" just a way to start talking?**
  - Calvin: it was real thirst, but He put her salvation ahead of His own needs. – https://www.studylight.org/commentary/john/4-7.html
  - Barnes: it was partly a way into a talk about faith. – https://www.studylight.org/commentary/john/4-7.html
  - Maclaren insists it was a genuine need, not just an icebreaker. – https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/4-7.htm
- Desiring God (John Piper): Jesus was willing to drink from the cup of a woman He knew to be disreputable. – https://www.desiringgod.org/messages/you-will-never-be-thirsty-again

**v. 8**
- Guzik: the disciples probably passed the woman on their way into town. – https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-4/
- Gill: the fact that they bought food there shows Jews did have *some* dealings with Samaritans. – https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/4-9.htm

**v. 9**
- **Who wrote the parenthesis ("For Jews do not associate…")?** Clarke and Gann say John added it for readers. Calvin and Gill say the woman said it; Calvin thinks she was mocking Him. – https://www.studylight.org/commentary/john/4-9.html ; https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/4-9.htm
- **What "no dealings" means:** Jews traded with Samaritans but would accept no favours from them and would not share vessels (Benson, Poole, Gill, Clarke). – https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/4-9.htm ; https://www.studylight.org/commentary/john/4-9.html
- **Background on the hostility** (Gill, Guzik, Don Stewart): its origins, the Samaritans' own temple on Gerizim, and the Jews destroying it around 128 BC. – https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/4-9.htm ; https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-4/ ; https://www.blueletterbible.org/faq/don_stewart/don_stewart_1319.cfm

**v. 10 – what is the "living water"?**
- **Literal sense:** spring or running water, as opposed to still water in a cistern (Clarke, Barnes, Barclay). – https://www.studylight.org/commentary/john/4-10.html
- Ellicott: experts "differ very widely" on what it means. – https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/4-10.htm
- **The views:**
  - The Holy Spirit: Calvin, Clarke and Constable (Constable also mentions cleansing grace). – https://www.studylight.org/commentary/john/4-10.html
  - Ellicott also reads it as the Spirit. – https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/4-10.htm
  - Eternal life, and finally God Himself: Maclaren. – https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/4-10.htm
  - Eternal life: Bridgeway. – https://www.studylight.org/commentary/john/4-10.html
  - Christ's teaching or grace: Barnes. – https://www.studylight.org/commentary/john/4-10.html
  - God's word: Coffman. – https://www.studylight.org/commentary/john/4-10.html
- Guzik:
  - Jesus raises three questions in her mind: about God's gift, about who He is, and about what He can give.
  - "If you knew more, you would pray more."
  - Old Testament roots: God as "fountain of living waters" (Jeremiah 2:13, quoted from Morris).
  – https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-4/

**vv. 11–12**
- She notices He has no bucket; the disciples probably took the leather one into town. – https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-4/
- Her question "Are you greater than Jacob?" could be sincere or cynical. That she later believed *may* suggest it was honest. – https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-4/

**vv. 13–14**
- Thirst stands for spiritual longing; only what Jesus gives satisfies. Drinking pictures faith: you receive rather than earn. Spurgeon is quoted: drinking is "even more simple than eating." – https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-4/
- Guzik's pastoral point: if you feel thirsty again, "drink again." It is an ongoing connection with Christ, not a single sip. The water also *becomes* a fountain inside the believer. – https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-4/
- Maclaren: like water, the fountain rises toward the eternal life it came from. – https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/4-10.htm
- I couldn't read any sources on whether "never thirst" means a believer can never fall away, the obvious place where Reformed and Wesleyan readers would differ.

**v. 15**
- Her request makes sense but isn't spiritual: she mainly wants to skip the daily trip to the well. – https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-4/
- Bengel: Jesus gave grace only when she herself asked for it. – https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/4-4.htm

**vv. 16–18**
- **Why "call your husband"?** Guzik gives two readings: having her husband present would make the long public talk more proper; and her sin had to be faced. – https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-4/
- Alford (cited by Guzik): the command is the first step in answering her request, because the Spirit's first work is to convict of sin. – https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-4/
- Spurgeon (cited by Guzik): Christ entered her life "by way of her conscience." – https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-4/
- Guzik: living together is not marriage, and calling something marriage doesn't make it so in Jesus' eyes. – https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-4/
- Piper calls her an "adulteress." – https://www.desiringgod.org/messages/you-will-never-be-thirsty-again

**v. 19**
- She is stunned that He knows her life. Spurgeon (cited by Guzik): it would have been better if she had seen she was a sinner. – https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-4/

**v. 20**
- Guzik: possibly a real stumbling block for her, but more likely a way to dodge the subject. Jesus cared more about winning a soul than an argument. – https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-4/
- Chuck Smith: Samaritans built their own worship centre on Gerizim and claimed Abraham offered Isaac there. – https://www.studylight.org/commentary/john/4-9.html

**v. 21**
- Worship will no longer be tied to one place. Dods (cited by Guzik) calls it one of Jesus' greatest announcements, made to "one sinful woman." – https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-4/
- Alford (cited by Guzik): the prophecy first came true in Samaria's conversion (Acts 8). – https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-4/
- Matthew Henry: Jewish worship was soon to be done away, and God revealed as Father of believers in every nation. – https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/4-4.htm

**v. 22**
- Samaritans accepted only the five books of Moses and mixed in other elements. In Morris's reading (cited by Guzik), Jesus sides firmly with the Jews. – https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-4/
- Matthew Henry: the message of salvation came to other nations *through* the Jews, and Christ rightly preferred Jewish worship. – https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/4-4.htm

**vv. 23–24**
- Guzik:
  - "In spirit": a concern with spiritual realities rather than places, sacrifices or outward ritual.
  - "In truth": worship that follows the whole of God's word, offered sincerely rather than for show.
  – https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-4/
- Matthew Henry: the human spirit, "influenced by the Holy Spirit," must worship God. – https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/4-4.htm
- Ellicott ties v. 4's "had to" to bringing "the spiritual service of the universal Father." – https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/4-4.htm
- Piper: the Father was seeking *her* worship. – https://www.desiringgod.org/messages/you-will-never-be-thirsty-again

**v. 25**
- Bruce (cited by Guzik under v. 10): later Samaritan liturgy speaks of the Taheb, their counterpart to the Messiah. – https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-4/

**v. 26**
- Jesus reveals Himself to a sinner. – https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-4/
- Maclaren: "I who speak to you am He" is the key to the earlier "Give me a drink": the eternal Word asked a poor woman for water. – https://biblehub.com/commentaries/john/4-7.htm

**v. 27**
- Barclay (cited by Guzik): rabbis avoided speaking to women in public. – https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-4/
- The disciples kept quiet out of reverence. Dods and Morris (cited by Guzik): they had learned He had good reasons for what He did. – https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/john-4/
- McGarvey (cited by Precept Austin): the passage breaks down barriers of race, gender and moral standing. – https://www.preceptaustin.org/john-4-commentary
